source_facts: MorrowSeat 6.0 is a synthetic event reservation product. This specification is authoritative for a box-office training primer about capacity and temporary holds. An event's capacity is its configured number of sellable seats. A hold is a temporary reservation of seats, not a completed sale. Each hold has an identifier called hold_id. Active holds consume availability. Availability equals capacity minus sold seats minus seats in active holds. The displayed field is named available. A successful sale converts a hold's seats to sold seats; the seats are not counted in both categories after conversion. A hold expires exactly 10 minutes after its creation time. Merely opening or refreshing the hold detail view does not renew it. Expiration releases the hold's seats back to availability. Confirmation is allowed only while the hold is active. A request to hold a quantity succeeds only if the full requested quantity is available; the product does not partially fill a hold request. A failed hold request reserves no seats. In the example event, capacity is 80, sold seats total 50, and active holds cover 20 seats, so available is 10. A request for 12 seats in that state fails as a whole. In a separate example, a hold created at 14:00 expires at 14:10; viewing it at 14:08 does not move the expiry. A hold that expires before confirmation cannot be confirmed as that same hold. Staff can consider a new request against current availability, but expiration does not promise that a replacement request will succeed. The event editor permits a capacity change only while the event is paused. This pause is required before saving the edit. A new capacity cannot be lower than the current sum of sold seats and seats in active holds, even while the event is paused. Pausing does not discard holds. The dashboard's available value updates on refresh rather than streaming live changes. A stale display is not an extra seat allocation, and the system evaluates a new hold against current availability. The page links to `hold-states.md` for hold-state terminology and `event-editor.md` for the event editor's UI reference. These links are supplemental; all necessary model facts are supplied here. This is a conceptual training document, not a pricing, refund, or event-reopening procedure. Organization, headings, and examples may change within that scope.

# How MorrowSeat counts seats

Box-office team leads use this primer when explaining reservations to new staff. Capacity is the configured number of sellable seats for an event. A customer conversation may involve a number visible on the dashboard, a temporary reservation, or a completed sale; those are related parts of the model, but they describe different things.

## After a sale

A successful sale converts the seats in a hold to sold seats. After conversion, those seats are not counted in both categories. This lets staff explain why completing a checkout does not consume the same seats twice. See [Hold states](hold-states.md) for the terminology used when discussing a reservation's state.

## Numbers from a training event

Suppose capacity is 80, sold seats total 50, and active holds cover 20 seats. The dashboard shows `available=10` after refresh. A request to hold 12 seats fails as a whole in this state; the system does not reserve the ten seats and leave the remaining two for later. The example represents one event at one point in time, not a standard capacity setting.

## Editing capacity

Team leads can use the event editor to save a new capacity. The new value cannot be lower than the current sum of sold seats and seats in active holds. [Event editor](event-editor.md) describes the controls used to enter the value. A capacity edit is therefore constrained by reservations as well as completed purchases.

## A clock example

A hold created at 14:00 expires at 14:10. Opening its detail view at 14:08 leaves the expiry at 14:10. If it expires before confirmation, staff cannot confirm that same hold afterward. They may consider a new request against current availability, but the earlier reservation does not guarantee that a replacement will succeed.

## What the dashboard means

The field `available` reports the seats remaining after sold seats and seats in active holds are subtracted from capacity. Its value updates on refresh, rather than streaming live changes. A number left on an old screen is not an additional seat allocation. A new hold request is evaluated against current availability.

## Temporary reservations

A hold temporarily reserves seats and is not a sale. Its identifier is called `hold_id`. Active holds consume availability while they exist. A request succeeds only when its full requested quantity is available; a failed request reserves no seats. Staff should distinguish a reservation identifier from evidence that a payment or sale has completed.

## Conditions for the actions above

Confirmation is allowed only while the hold is active. The event must be paused before a capacity edit can be saved. Pausing does not discard holds, and it does not remove the lower bound on capacity described above. These conditions apply even when a staff member is looking at a dashboard that has not yet been refreshed.

## Expiration

A hold expires exactly 10 minutes after its creation time. Opening or refreshing the detail view does not renew it. Expiration releases its seats back to availability. The distinction between elapsed time and staff activity is important when a customer asks whether staying on the reservation screen will keep seats reserved. This page explains the capacity model; it does not cover pricing or refunds.
